_meta.title: mPulse Query API Reference Catalog
_meta.purpose: Pre-resolved names and behaviors so an agent never re-discovers valid metric/timer/dimension values by trial and error.
_meta.generated_by: Empirically verified vs live mpulse MCP (app=app-a) + Akamai TechDocs endpoint reference pages + Akamai cli-mpulse; bandwith-block spelling and custom-dimension usage confirmed by app owner.
_meta.custom_metric_source: App-specific CUSTOM metrics/timers are not in these enums. Get them from Repository/Objects API domain['custom_metrics'] (github.com/akamai/mPulseAPI.jl) or the dashboard report-builder.

confidence_legend.verified_docs: From the Akamai endpoint reference enum lists.
confidence_legend.verified_live: Confirmed against the live API in this environment.

CRITICAL_same_metric_different_name_per_.note: A physical metric is named ONE way for timers-metrics (CamelCase) and a DIFFERENT way for metrics-by-dimension (snake_case). They don't even share a root. Pick the name for the endpoint you're calling.
CRITICAL_same_metric_different_name_per_.note_TotalRequestCount: TotalRequestCount is NOT in the timers-metrics docs enum (its Total* group lists 8 items, matching the doc's '97' count) yet it RETURNS a valid series in the live API (verified: returns a valid series). Treat as working-but-undocumented. Per-content-type counts (PageRequestCount, JsRequestCount, ImgRequestCount, ...) ARE documented.

metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.endpoint: timers-metrics (also summary/histogram/by-minute use the `timer` param family, not this)
metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.multiple: The API allows repeating metric= and timer= params. Via the MCP `query` tool, params is a dict so you can't repeat a key -> one metric per call. (A JSON list is silently ignored -> only PageLoad returns.)
metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.prefixes: Bcn(beacon), Css, Font, Html, Img(image), Js, Other, Page, Total(all), Xhr. Suffixes: RequestCount, TransferSize, DecodedBodySize, CompressionRatio, ByteCompressionRatio, BrowserCacheHitRatio, CdnCacheHitRatio, CdnEdgeTime, OriginTime.
metrics_for_timers_metrics__metric_param.param_name: metric (singular; repeat the key for multiple, e.g. metric=Beacons&metric=PageLoad)

metrics_for_metrics_by_dimension__metric.multiple: Comma-separated list in ONE `metrics` param, e.g. metrics=beacons,largest_contentful_paint (verified live).
constraints: apperror_message/apperror_code/apperror_source/apperror_type dimensions only support errors_per_page (+ AppErrors, AppErrorsPct).
page_group, full_url, network_error_code dimensions do NOT support: session, session_length, session_duration, bounce_rate.
network_error_code, beacon_type dimensions do NOT support: errors_per_page.
metrics_for_metrics_by_dimension__metric.metric_singular_ignored: passing `metric` (singular) is silently ignored -> app-default columns are returned instead. Use `metrics` (plural).

extra_params.limit: int; results come pre-sorted (native API limit, 1-100)

metrics_for_metrics_by_dimension__metric.mixing_note: Mixing count metrics (beacons) with percentile timers can yield a null column; timer/percentile metrics together are safest.

timers_for_timer_param.endpoints: timers-metrics, summary, histogram, by-minute (and timer-by-* reports)
timers_for_timer_param.note: Unrecognized `timer` SILENTLY falls back to PageLoad (no error) - always check response series id == requested name. For custom timers use custom-timer=<name>, or timer=CustomTimer[0-9] by index. Invalid custom-timer DOES 400.
timers_for_timer_param.param_name: timer (singular; repeat the key for multiple)

drilldown_filter_params.note: Hyphenated. Used to FILTER any report. NOTE the API misspells bandwidth as 'bandwith-block' (missing d, verified live). Custom dimensions filter via custom-dimension-<label>=<value>, e.g. custom-dimension-branch=uk to filter to branch=uk. <label> = the custom dimension name, lowercased with spaces replaced by underscores.

metrics_by_dimension__dimension_split_en.note: underscored. The value for the `dimension` param in metrics-by-dimension (what to split BY). This enum is BUILT-IN only and NOT exhaustive: a CUSTOM DIMENSION name can be used directly as the dimension value, e.g. dimension=branch to break a metric down by the custom 'branch' dimension. There is no API to list an app's custom dimensions, so the user must supply the exact custom name.

dimension_values__dimension_enum.note: underscored. Valid `dimension` values for the dimension-values query. connection_type is NOT here -> that's why dimension-values with connection-type 400s. (The MCP accepts hyphenated aliases like beacon-type/device-type and maps them.) CUSTOM DIMENSIONS ARE NOT ALLOWED here (built-in only); use metrics-by-dimension to break down by a custom dimension.

beacon-type.note: 'page view' has a space. Live data for app-a currently shows only 'page view' and 'xhr'.

percentile.note: one value per query; p50 & p75 need two calls

timezone.note: Java-parseable names e.g. US/Eastern, Europe/London, Asia/Shanghai

date.note: one calendar day; current day assumed if date and date-comparator both absent

date_comparator.note: Between needs date-start & date-end; Last needs trailing-seconds. ThisMonth = current month to date.

date_start_end.note: For Between. Docs: date-end must be GREATER than date-start. Live behavior: date-end is EXCLUSIVE (June = start 2026-06-01, end 2026-07-01). Multi-day ranges auto-coarsen buckets (~2d hourly, ~30d daily).

items: Invalid `timer` or `metric` name -> silent fallback to PageLoad (no error). Validate response series id == requested name.
`metric` as a JSON list is ignored via the MCP -> only default PageLoad returns. Pass a single string per call.

timers-metrics `latest` = aggregate over the WHOLE selected period (e.g. Beacons daily latest == total n; percentile metric latest == period-wide percentile). history[] is the per-bucket series. For a monthly p75/p50 read `latest`, do not average daily history.
date-end is EXCLUSIVE for Between despite docs saying 'greater than'.
dimension naming differs by context: FILTER params are hyphenated (beacon-type); the split `dimension` value is underscored (beacon_type).
Param misspelling is REAL (verified live): the bandwidth filter param is `bandwith-block` (missing 'd'); `bandwidth-block` does not work.
Custom dimensions: filter with custom-dimension-<label>=<value>; split with metrics-by-dimension dimension=<custom_name>. No API lists them -> user supplies exact names.
metrics-by-dimension: the metric param is `metrics` (PLURAL, comma-separated). `metric` (singular) is silently ignored -> app-default columns returned.

metrics-by-dimension computes percentiles (timer p75 by dimension matches timers-metrics). Mixing a count metric (beacons) with a percentile can yield a null column; keep timer/percentile metrics together.

Multiple values for repeat-style params (metric, timer, filters, custom-dimension-*) must be a JSON LIST -> the client expands to repeated query keys. Only metrics-by-dimension `metrics` is comma-separated.
metric-per-page-load-time uses a single `metric` with a distinct enum (BounceRate + CustomMetric0-9).

drilldown_combination_rule.rule: Unsupported dimension combos return EMPTY data, not an error -> empty may mean 'combo unsupported', not 'no traffic'.

worked_example.goal: app-a monthly p75 asset requests/page, page-view beacons, June 2026
worked_example.read: response series where id=='TotalRequestCount' -> latest (the period p75 value)

custom_dimensions.split_usage: metrics-by-dimension dimension=<custom_name>  e.g. dimension=branch (metric broken down by 'branch')
custom_dimensions.label_rule: <label> is the custom dimension name lowercased, spaces -> underscores. Use .NONE to match beacons with no value.
custom_dimensions.enumeration: No API returns an app's defined custom dimensions. The user must know/type the exact name. Built-in dimension enums here do NOT include custom dimensions.

custom_dimension_support.note: Custom dimensions (e.g. 'branch') are accepted ONLY as the metrics-by-dimension `dimension` split value. dimension-values and dimension-over-time accept BUILT-IN dimensions only (a custom name returns empty/400 -> wasted call). To analyze a custom dimension, use metrics-by-dimension with dimension=<custom_name>.

metrics_for_metric_per_page_load_time__m.note: Completely different metric name space from the other endpoints; only one metric per call.

parameter_mechanics.how_to_pass: Via the MCP `query` tool: pass a JSON LIST for a repeat-style param (e.g. "custom-dimension-branch": ["uk","us"]) and the client expands it to repeated keys. Pass a comma-joined STRING for `metrics` (e.g. "metrics": "beacons,largest_contentful_paint"). Single-value params take a scalar.
